question: A 27-year-old man is brought to the emergency department because of weakness, headache, and vomiting for 40 minutes. He is an amateur chef and his symptoms started 10 minutes after he ingested pufferfish that he had prepared. On arrival, he is lethargic. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 120/min, respirations are 8/min, and blood pressure is 92/64 mm Hg. He is intubated and mechanical ventilation is begun. Intravenous fluid resuscitation is started. The cause of this patient's condition exerts its effect by which of the following mechanisms of action?

options.opa: Decrease in cell membrane permeability to sodium ions
options.opb: Increase in cell membrane permeability to chloride ions
options.opc: Decrease in cell membrane permeability to calcium ions
options.opd: Decrease in cell membrane permeability to potassium ions
options.ope: Increase in cell membrane permeability to calcium ions

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Ingestion of pufferfish -> Tetrodotoxin exposure -> Blockade of sodium channels -> Decrease in cell membrane permeability to sodium ions -> 95% CHAIN: Ingestion of pufferfish -> Tetrodotoxin exposure -> Inhibition of action potentials -> Decrease in cell membrane permeability to sodium ions -> 95%
analysis: The symptoms and presentation described are consistent with tetrodotoxin poisoning, which is found in pufferfish. Tetrodotoxin exerts its effect by blocking sodium channels, leading to a decrease in cell membrane permeability to sodium ions. This results in the symptoms of weakness, headache, vomiting, and respiratory distress seen in this patient.
